agent_research.summary: Markets entered a dense policy week on a cautious footing: US equities remained elevated (Nasdaq 26,169, Dow 52,362, S&P 500 7,624) with the VIX near 19.5, while crude stayed firm (WTI 101.76, Brent 115.81) and gold held a defensive bid around 4,038. The US 10-year Treasury sat at 5.00% with yields broadly steady as investors balanced AI-related credit unease against safe-haven demand. Hormuz shipping risk and thin spare oil capacity keep the energy backdrop tense, even as LNG flows through the strait have improved. AI and private-credit headlines—stressed neocloud names and large debt raises for chips and data centres—are feeding the bid for duration and quality. Surveys point to a Bank of Canada move toward 2.50% on 28 October; Japan is expected to hold this week but sound hawkish after September’s call-rate step-up. New Zealand inflation could not be verified, so NZ-specific new risk stays off the board. Next: Federal Reserve and Bank of Canada decisions on 28 October, Bank of Japan messaging, megacap earnings, and whether oil and AI-credit jitters spill into broader risk appetite.
